attribution.note: Zitron's own words on his own blog. The lead-generation capability is correctly kept as Benioff's claim, and Zitron's own claim is that no information exists.

semantics.note: The proposition is faithful and narrowed correctly to 'I can find no information'. The 'allegedly' attribution to Benioff is kept. It is a present-tense observation, not a forecast.

contract.note: The plain reading is fair and ordinary: 'when it will do so' means when customers can use the sales functions, and 'how' means how those functions work. Under this reading a scheduled conference reveal (TDX, March 7) does not count as availability, so the result depends on that interpretation.

evidence.note: Benioff's Feb 8, 2023 teaser confirms the attributed claim. It gives no workflow and no availability date.
A consultancy's account from Feb 14, 2023 says there was no official press release yet, only hints. It names March 7 TDX as the launch event, which is a reveal, not customer availability.

On the March 1 earnings call, Benioff gave integration plans and a March 7–8 presentation date. This is relevant to a broad reading of 'when', but it gives no availability and no explanation of how Einstein would generate leads or close deals.
Salesforce's own release of March 7, 2023 says the product is in closed pilot. It comes after the assessed period, so it cannot show what was public by March 6.

reviews.rationale: Records before the post (e1, e2, e3) show only teasers, integration claims and a reveal date. None gives customer availability or explains how Einstein would generate leads or close deals. Even the March 7 release (e4) offered only a closed pilot. The packet admits it cannot prove absolute absence. Still, both the contemporary account and the CEO's own remarks fit the claim that no such information was public.
